subject.title: Install ClawHub packages for new Claw agents

question: Is explicit `claws add --yes --plan-integrity` consent the intended sufficient authorization for installing or reusing a process-wide shared-host plugin from an agent-oriented Claw flow?
rationale: The implementation deliberately keeps plugins process-wide rather than agent-isolated, and discussion contains competing boundary expectations; this policy choice cannot be resolved mechanically from tests alone.

options.title: Accept exact-plan shared-host consent
options.body: Treat the displayed package action, digest, runtime id, and owner state as sufficient explicit authorization while the feature remains experimental.

options.title: Require a distinct host-level grant
options.body: Keep skills installable from the agent flow but require a separate host or Scout-level authorization before shared-plugin mutation.

options.title: Pause plugin mutation
options.body: Merge no shared-plugin lifecycle path until the RFC or product owner defines the durable authorization model.

recommendation.title: Require a distinct host-level grant
recommendation.body: Keep skills installable from the agent flow but require a separate host or Scout-level authorization before shared-plugin mutation.

likelyOwner.reason: Their review established the package lifecycle safety requirements and is the strongest supplied routing signal for this remaining design decision.
